public_body: Minuteman Regional Vocational Technical School Committee
overall: The Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by convening its March 24 meeting in a room other than the one on the notice, but cured it the same day; the remote access and other claims were not violations.

allegations.summary: Committee convened its March 24 meeting in a room other than the one stated on the notice, with no notice of the change.
allegations.key_passage: the Committee nonetheless violated the Open Meeting Law by convening its meeting in a location other than that specified on the meeting notice.

allegations.summary: The location violation was cured the same day when the Committee moved to the posted room and restarted the meeting within ten minutes.
allegations.key_passage: That is exactly what the Committee did when it moved its meeting to the proper location—which was set up for a meeting to begin shortly—within ten minutes of the posted start time and re-started the meeting from the beginning.

allegations.summary: Zoom access allegedly did not start until 6:00 P.M. and had no audio or consistent video, despite the notice promising remote access.
The full meeting was allegedly not available remotely, and the remote portion was audio only with no video feed.
allegations.key_passage: Chapter 20 allows public bodies to provide the public with “adequate, alternative” access to meetings instead of providing in-person access but does not require public bodies to provide “adequate, alternative” access if in-person access is provided.

allegations.summary: Committee allegedly entered executive session without first convening in an open session the public could attend.
allegations.key_passage: This fact, combined with the Committee initially beginning its meeting in a room other than the public meeting space, suggest that the Committee did not view the executive session convening procedures as part of the public meeting.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint; the AG noted concern that open session minutes omit the executive session purpose and the roll call vote.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Committee that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
